leads.summary: A Vfio state set outside the menu can trigger deletion of administrator-managed sleep and service files
leads.consequence: supergfxctl 5.2.7 accepts explicit Vfio (-m Vfio) when vfio_enable is enabled, so this arm is not limited to the Omarchy sleep hook. A user deliberately using Vfio for a guest can accept a prompt that only mentions returning to Hybrid and rebooting; the arm removes both named files, even when either file has non-Omarchy contents or is a root-managed symlink, without ownership/content checks or backup. Reboot removes the VFIO mode as requested, but unrelated custom hooks or service delay are lost. On the next run -g reports Hybrid, so there is no undo path; Hybrid -> Integrated installs the stock Omarchy versions rather than the custom files. The existing Integrated arm already has the same deletion, but this PR newly exposes it from an independently configured Vfio state. Consider recognizing the installed Omarchy files (or offering an explicit destructive warning) before cleanup.
leads.triage: factual but pre-existing: the Integrated arm deletes the same paths unconditionally; deliberate Vfio users are confirm-gated. Dropped as low value

leads.summary: Valid, manually reformatted supergfxd JSON makes the new Vfio recovery silently fail or discard other settings
leads.consequence: If an administrator reformats the config while supergfxd is running, `-g` may still report its in-memory Vfio, while the file is valid JSON with whitespace before the colon or with multiple keys on the mode's line. `sed -i` returns zero even when its fixed literal does not match: for `"mode" : "Vfio"`, no mode change occurs, yet the new arm removes the hook and drop-in and schedules a reboot. On reboot supergfxd loads Vfio again. For a one-line object, the greedy `.*` consumes every later field, leaving only `"mode": "Hybrid"`; upstream's required fields fail deserialization and its startup recreates defaults, losing custom vfio_enable, hotplug_type and other choices. If the config is absent when the daemon is already running, sed fails but the script lacks set -e and still removes support files and schedules reboot, without an error status. This is a limitation copied from Integrated's old edit, but introduced into this recovery arm. Validate the format and replacement and fail before cleanup/reboot (prefer a structured JSON update).
leads.triage: partly verified: sed status is unchecked (Opus run 3 confirms). Reformatted-config cases dropped: supergfxd rewrites the config with to_string_pretty at every start and switch (config.rs load/write), so non-canonical shapes need a manual edit while the daemon runs. Only the unchecked-sed optional note is published

leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1; added fact that the #11843 test expects Integrated, verified in intake/related-11843.diff lines 151-152; published

leads.summary: Open #9332 replaces this entire supergfxctl feature with cardwire and does not retain the Vfio arm

@@ -79,3 +79,55 @@

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- With a saved `Vfio` mode, confirming rewrites the mode to `Hybrid`, removes the hook and drop-in, and reboots; declining changes nothing (stubbed `sudo`, `gum` and reboot).
- supergfxd 5.2.7 reads `/etc/supergfxd.conf` only at startup and writes it only then and after a successful switch, so the edit holds until the reboot (source).
- From `Vfio`, `supergfxctl -m Hybrid` prints "You must change to Integrated before you can change to Hybrid" and exits 1, although the daemon still attempts the switch in the background; editing the config and rebooting does not depend on that live driver unload (source).
- `hybrid-gpu-test.sh`, `hw-hybrid-gpu-test.sh`, `system-sleep-ownership-migration-test.sh` and `unowned-system-paths-test.sh` pass at this head and with it merged onto current `quattro` (the last one with an `omarchy-pkgs` checkout).

**Optional notes:**
- Users reaching this arm normally came from `Integrated` (supergfxd will not switch `Hybrid` straight to `Vfio`); the arm sends them to `Hybrid` and removes the Integrated support files, so returning to `Integrated` takes a second toggle and reboot. The prompt could say so, or offer both targets with `gum choose`.
- Like the `Integrated` arm, this arm does not check that `sudo sed` succeeded (no `set -e`): when `sudo sed` fails (for example after a mistyped password), a stubbed run still removed both files and rebooted with the saved mode left at `Vfio`. Checking the edit before cleanup would avoid that pointless reboot.
- `Fixes #11868` makes GitHub close #11868 on merge, although the description says its hook half is still open; `Refs #11868` would keep it open.
</details>
